text_summary.body: Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king's food and wine and asked the official's steward to test the four youths on vegetables and water for ten days; afterwards they looked healthier than the others and were allowed to continue.

setting.body: A private episode within the court training described in Daniel 1.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4RSRHMKXKQME68JMA71TAZ6
constraints.textual_assertion: the steward whom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel

competing_reconstructions.label: Ritual purity (kashrut)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Daniel avoided food that broke Jewish dietary or ritual-slaughter laws.

competing_reconstructions.label: Food and wine offered to Babylonian gods
competing_reconstructions.summary: The royal provisions had been offered to idols.

competing_reconstructions.label: Refusing covenant fellowship and dependence on the king
competing_reconstructions.summary: Eating at the king's table implied loyalty to and dependence on the Babylonian king.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik commends Daniel's resolve formed in advance and his courteous, testable proposal, and treats the outcome as God's blessing on faithfulness.

not_applicable.geography: Location is the royal court, already recorded on the parent event.
